meta.title: Feature Engineering and Pipelines
meta.thesis: Feature Engineering and Pipelines is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A churn model depends on billing, product, and support features that refresh daily. By the end, they should be able to build or review feature pipeline contract with leakage, freshness, and ownership checks, measure fresh features available before scoring, and catch the failure where a feature leaks future behavior into the training set.

mentalMap.title: Feature Engineering and Pipelines: mental map
mentalMap.caption: Build leakage-safe feature pipelines: define raw data, fit train-only transforms, compose columns, test leakage, and monitor feature behavior.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: Feature engineering turns raw data into model inputs, and pipelines keep those transformations repeatable and evaluation-safe.

modules.title: Features are the model view of raw data
modules.sub: Raw columns become signals only after careful definition.
modules.summary: Feature engineering defines what the model can see.
objectives: Turn raw support data into candidate features.
Explain why feature definitions need lineage.
Separate available-at-prediction-time fields from future fields.

blocks.title: A feature is a promise about what the model may know

spans.text: Problem anchor: predict whether a support ticket is urgent. Raw data includes ticket text, customer plan, account age, previous ticket count, agent notes, and final resolution time. Resolution time is tempting because it predicts urgency, but it is known only after the ticket is handled. It is leakage, not a usable feature.
Good feature engineering states source, timestamp, transformation, allowed use, and owner. The model can only learn from the view you give it.

blocks.analogy: Features are ingredients laid out before cooking; future facts are ingredients from tomorrow.

spans.text: Feature: recent_ticket_count_30d. Source: ticket table. Time rule: count tickets opened before current ticket timestamp. Transform: log1p count. Owner: support analytics. Leakage check: excludes current ticket resolution and future tickets.

blocks.title: Feature availability
blocks.prompt: Why is final resolution time a bad training feature for ticket-priority prediction?

options.text: It is numeric, and numeric features are never allowed.
It is unavailable when the model must make the prediction.
It would make the model too interpretable.

blocks.explanation: Features must exist at prediction time.

modules.title: Fit transformers on train only
modules.sub: Scalers, imputers, and encoders can leak evaluation information.
modules.summary: Learned preprocessing must be fit on training data and applied to validation/test.
objectives: Use pipelines to enforce train-only fitting.

spans.text: A scaler learns means and variances. An imputer learns replacement values. A category encoder learns category mapping. If these are fit on all rows before splitting, validation and test information has influenced training. A pipeline helps by fitting preprocessing inside cross-validation or train-only fit calls.

The team standardizes account_age using the mean from all tickets, including validation. The validation distribution has a launch-week surge of new accounts. The train features now contain a hint of validation distribution. The effect may be small, but the discipline is simple: fit preprocessing on train only.

modules.title: Column pipelines keep preprocessing repeatable
modules.sub: Different column types need different transforms in one artifact.
modules.summary: ColumnTransformer and Pipeline make preprocessing and model fitting reproducible.
objectives: Keep preprocessing tied to the model.
Review pipeline steps as a production artifact.

blocks.title: The pipeline is the model input contract

spans.text: A support-ticket model may scale numeric features, one-hot encode product category, and pass text-derived counts through unchanged. A pipeline ties those transformations to the model so training, validation, and inference use the same steps.

cells.text: validation/test distribution leak if fit globally
distance or coefficient distortion if inconsistent
cannot reproduce predictions if preprocessing is separate

modules.title: Leakage hides in time, targets, and aggregates
modules.sub: The hardest feature bugs look like impressive validation scores.
modules.summary: Leakage checks should be coded and reviewed like tests.
objectives: Predict why target-derived features inflate metrics.

blocks.title: Leakage-safe preprocessing pipeline skeleton
blocks.code:
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

numeric = ["account_age_days", "recent_ticket_count_30d", "text_length"]
categorical = ["plan_tier", "product_area"]

numeric_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
    ("scale", StandardScaler()),
])
category_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
    ("onehot", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")),
])

preprocess = ColumnTransformer([
    ("num", numeric_pipe, numeric),
    ("cat", category_pipe, categorical),
])

model = Pipeline([
    ("preprocess", preprocess),
    ("clf", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)),
])

# Correct pattern after splitting:
# model.fit(X_train, y_train)
# validation_score = model.score(X_val, y_val)

spans.text: The pipeline learns imputations, scaling, encodings, and model weights only when fit is called on training data. Validation rows are transformed using the learned training transforms.

predictThenReveal.prompt: Predict the leakage risk if SimpleImputer and StandardScaler are fit on the full dataset before train/validation split.
predictThenReveal.answer: Validation statistics influence the training representation. Metrics can look better than deployment reality because preprocessing saw information from the evaluation rows.

spans.text: Checklist: split before fit; learned transforms are inside Pipeline or ColumnTransformer; target-derived and future-derived features are excluded; aggregations use only past data; unknown categories are handled; and feature definitions include source and timestamp rules.

modules.title: Monitoring keeps feature contracts honest
modules.sub: A feature pipeline can drift even when code does not change.
modules.summary: Production feature quality needs data checks, drift alerts, and owner review.
objectives: Name feature drift and schema drift.
Plan monitoring for missingness, ranges, and categories.
Connect pipeline checks to model maintenance.

spans.text: After deployment, product_area may get new categories, text_length may shift after a UI change, or recent_ticket_count_30d may break when an event pipeline changes. Monitor missingness, value ranges, category rates, freshness, and prediction slices. A feature owner should know when a contract changes.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Treat feature definitions, pipelines, and monitors as one artifact.
blocks.useWhen: Use this approach for any ML system where raw product data must be transformed before modeling.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid one-off notebook features, all-data preprocessing, and unowned aggregates that cannot be reproduced at inference.

blocks.title: Feature monitoring
blocks.prompt: A new product_area category appears in production. What should a robust pipeline do?

options.text: Handle the unknown category safely and alert owners if rates shift materially.
Refit using production test labels automatically.

blocks.explanation: Pipelines need runtime contracts as well as training code.

ai.label: AI
ai.laymanDefinition: Software systems that perform tasks associated with human intelligence.
ai.technicalNote: In these foundations lessons, AI is the broad field; the concrete mechanisms are models, data, objectives, and evaluation loops.

ml.label: ML
ml.laymanDefinition: A branch of AI where systems learn patterns from data instead of only following hand-written rules.
ml.technicalNote: ML work is defined by training data, features, models, objectives, validation, and deployment constraints.

model.label: Model
model.laymanDefinition: A learned or configured function that maps inputs to predictions, scores, clusters, or generated outputs.
model.technicalNote: Model choice encodes assumptions such as linearity, distance, tree splits, capacity, or sequential reward.

loss.label: Loss
loss.laymanDefinition: A numerical training signal that measures how wrong a prediction is for a task.
loss.technicalNote: Loss drives optimization; it is not the same as product quality, fairness, or final generalization.

generalization.label: Generalization
generalization.laymanDefinition: The ability of a model to perform well on examples it did not train on.
generalization.technicalNote: Generalization is checked with validation/test data, leakage audits, and slice monitoring.

pipeline.label: Pipeline
pipeline.laymanDefinition: A repeatable sequence of data transforms, feature steps, model fitting, and evaluation or inference.
pipeline.technicalNote: Pipelines prevent train/test leakage and keep preprocessing identical between training and production.
